Condition_A_Matched.censoring_note: C did not cross tau=0.80 within 50 epochs in any run (T_C > 50). S crossed in 3/5 runs at epoch 1.

binary_crossing_tests.pairing_description: Observations paired by random model seed on identical data instance.

Condition_A_Matched.statistical_conclusion: Under matched signals, S crossed threshold in 3/5 runs vs 0/5 for C. Because observations are paired by model seed, an exact McNemar binomial test yields one-sided p = 0.1250 (two-sided p = 0.2500); an unpaired Fisher exact test yields one-sided p = 0.0833 (two-sided p = 0.1667). Neither binary test achieves statistical significance at alpha = 0.05 due to power constraints with N = 5. At epoch 1, S shows a statistically significant initial lead (Acc S = 83.04% vs Acc C = 62.21%, paired t(4) = 4.19, p = 0.0138), reflecting first-order gradient alignment before loss reduction.

Condition_B_Complex_Dominant.censoring_note: S did not cross tau=0.80 within 50 epochs in any run (T_S > 50). C crossed at epoch 1 in all runs.

binary_crossing_tests.pairing_description: Observations paired by random model seed on identical data instance.

Condition_B_Complex_Dominant.statistical_conclusion: When complex signal quality dominates, learning order decisively inverts: C crossed at epoch 1 in 5/5 runs (100%), while S failed to cross in any run (0/5, T_S > 50). The paired McNemar exact test yields one-sided p = 0.03125 (statistically significant at alpha = 0.05). Final counterfactual accuracy heavily favors C (96.95% vs 50.80% chance level, paired t(4) = 78.42, p = 1.58e-07).

Condition_Comparison_A_vs_B.note_on_reported_t: The actual Welch two-sample test statistic is t = 19.17 (df = 4.43, p = 1.96e-05) and the paired test across matched seeds is t(4) = 17.79 (p = 5.87e-05). Any historical citation of 't(4) = 48.61' was unsupported.
Condition_Comparison_A_vs_B.interpretation: Statistically significant reversal of feature reliance between Condition A and Condition B (+49.75% margin shift).
